'''Frédérique Battin-Leclerc''' (born 1964) is a French chemist who studies [[combustion]], particularly gas-phase combustion of [[hydrocarbon]]s including [[biofuel]]s, in order to develop cleaner-burning automotive fuels.{{r|repub}} She is a director of research for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS), affiliated with the Laboratoire Réactions et Génie des Procédés in [[Nancy, France]].

==Education and career==
Battin-Leclerc was born in 1964. She earned an engineering degree from the [[École nationale supérieure des industries chimiques]] in Nancy in 1987, completed a Ph.D. at the [[National Polytechnic Institute of Lorraine]] in Nancy in 1991, and earned a [[habilitation]] at the National Polytechnic Institute of Lorraine in 1997.{{r|cand}}

She has been a researcher for the CNRS since 1991.{{r|cand}}

==Recognition==
Battin-Leclerc won the [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 2010,{{r|repub}} and was named as a knight in the [[Ordre national du Mérite]] in 2012.{{r|cand}}

She was elected to the inaugural 2018 class of Fellows of [[The Combustion Institute]], "for innovative research on the formulation of detailed chemical mechanisms for complex practical fuels".{{r|fci}}

She was the 2022 recipient of the [[Polanyi Medal]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].{{r|polanyi}}
